docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Welcome to my personal hub for Digimon Story: Time Stranger modding tutorials, documentation, and resources. If you have any questions, suggestions, or just want to chat, join the Digimon Modding Discord community.

Special thanks to everyone whose information, guides, tools, and research made this project possible.

docs.title: Digimon Time Stranger Textures
docs.text:
All the textures are located in the "images" folder.

Although they use the .img extension, they are actually .dds files with the wrong file extension. To edit them, simply rename each file and change its extension .dds. Example: chr050a01.img → chr050a01.dds

Changing the texture format back to .img after editing them is not required. The game can read them as .dds.

Info

If you can't see file extensions, open Windows Explorer and go to View → Show → File name extensions.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• Paint.net, to convert images to dds. You can use other programs, but this one has all the settings we need for Time Stranger.
  • Any image editing tool, like Photopea (free), Gimp (free), Affinity (free) or Adobe Photoshop (paid).
  • If you want a lightweight dds image viewer, install IrfanView (+ plugins). It can read dds files with img extension without having to rename them. To turn off the "incorrect extension" popup, go to Options → Properties/Settings → File Handling → Ask to rename if incorrect extension.
  • To batch-rename files, you can use Advanced Renamer.

Info

In order open dds files with Photoshop, you must install the Nvidia Texture Tools Exporter plugin

docs.title: Texture sizes
docs.text:
• Textures dimensions must be a power of 2 (256x256 px, 512x512 px, 1024x1024 px, 2048x2048 px, etc).
  • Usually, smaller Digimon (Babies and Rookies) use 1024×1024 px textures, while larger Digimon use 2048×2048 px textures. However, some Digimon break this pattern. For example, Monochromon uses 1024×1024 px textures. Ultimately, the choice is up to you.
  • Dot sprites are 32x32 px.
  • Profile pictures are 512x512 px.

docs.title: The DDS format
docs.text: .dds textures have three crucial parameters: compression, encoding and mipmaps.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
There are mainly three compression methods:

  • BC1: small file size, low quality, transparency with jagged edges.
  • BC7: big file size, best quality, smooth transparency.
  • None: only used by dot sprites.

Whether to use BC1 or BC7 depends on your needs. If a texture has transparency, use BC7, otherwise, use BC1. Avoid using BC7 textures whenever possible, since they are are twice the size of BC1 textures, and in most cases, you will barely notice the difference. Learning how to optimize your mods is key, since as you continue adding content, the file size can increase considerably.

docs.title: Encoding
docs.text:
.dds files have two encoding methods:

  • sRGB: used for colors (base color, emission map and environment map).
  • Linear: used for UI and data (normal maps, light maps, etc.).

Using the wrong encoding results in bright or washed-out colors, or in textures not appearing at all.

docs.title: Mipmaps
docs.text: Mipmaps are smaller versions of the texture stored inside the .dds file. They make the game use less RAM, and prevent jagged lines and shimmering when an image is scaled down or tilted. However, they increase the file size. Using mipmaps is optional, but highly encouraged for icons and profile pictures.

docs.title: Base color/Diffuse map
docs.text:
Agumon's base color textures (chr050a01.img, chr050b01.img and chr050p01.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps BC1 or BC7 sRGB Optional

Also called diffuse texture or diffuse color. It contains basic colors, with minimal lighting and effects. For most recolors, you will only edit this texture. Some models have multiple color textures. For example, Agumon has three: one for the body, one for the eye lids and one for the iris. The color of the texture can also be adjusted with the "DSTS-DiffuseAlpha" material node in Blender (it has 4 values, representing red, green, blue and alpha values).

docs.title: Normal map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "n".

Agumon's normal map texture (chr050a01n.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps BC1 or BC7 Linear Optional

Creates the illusion of bumps and other fine details without adding extra geometry. It's not much different from normal maps in other games. For a more detailed explanation, check out this Wikipedia article. We usually don't modify these textures unless we're creating new models. To generate custom Normal Maps, you can use NormalMap Online or Gimp (filter → generic → normal map).

docs.title: Light map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "l".

Agumon's light map texture (chr050a01l.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps BC1 or BC7 Linear Optional

Controls the intensity and position of lights and shadows. It's usually a black and white version of the base color texture in the red channel (with some extra contrast), and the other channels completely white, giving a cyan look. Here's a video showing how to create a light map using Photoshop or Photopea (you can use any image editing software):

Steps
  1. Add a hue/saturation adjustment layer and set the saturation to -100.
  2. Make the dark parts darker and the white parts lighter. You can use a "levels" adjustment layer or a "brightness/contrast" adjustment layer.
  3. Add a "channel mixer" adjustment layer. Set the green constant to +200 and the blue constant to +200.
  4. Save the image.

docs.title: Material map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "m" (not to be confused with emission maps, which end with "em").

Agumon's material map texture (chr050a01m.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps Always BC7 Linear Optional
  • The "red" channel of the texture controls glossiness.
  • The "green" channel of the texture controls metallic reflection.
  • The "blue" channel is unknown. It's only used by a handful of models, such as Matadormon (chr031), and editing it doesn't appear to have any visible effect.
  • The "alpha" (or "transparency") channel of the texture controls rim light intensity.

All three effects can be used simultaneously.

docs.title: Glossiness
docs.text:
Also called "specular", "reflectiveness" or "reflectivity". Adds a simple reflection to the material. The shape of the highlight is controlled by the shadow map. Areas painted white on the texture are reflective, while areas painted black have no reflections. This is commonly used for materials such as teeth, leather, horns, and claws.

Glossiness examples

(Default material map: zipper, nose and claws are glossy)

(Custom material map: Full body is glossy)

docs.title: Metallic reflection
docs.text:
Adds a metallic effect to the material by using environment maps. Areas painted white on the texture appear metallic, while areas painted black have no metallic reflection.

Metallic reflection examples

(Default material map: only the zipper is metallic)

(Custom material map: full body is metallic)

docs.title: Rim light intensity
docs.text:
Controls the opacity of the rim light that appears around the model, also known as Fresnel effect or inner glow. Areas painted white on the texture have a fully visible rim light, while areas painted black have no rim light. Most models use dark gray values in the alpha channel, making the rim light only slightly visible.

Rim light examples

(Default material map: rim light barely visible)

(Custom material map: rim light fully visible)

The color of the rim light can be adjusted in Blender using the "DSTS-InnerGrowBColor" material node. It has three values representing the red, green, and blue channels. The size of the rim light can also be adjusted in Blender using the "DSTS-InnerGrowABase" material node.

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
Here's a video showing how to create a material map (where Agumon has glossy and metallic nails and teeth) using Photopea (you can use any image editing software):

Steps
  1. Open the image and create a folder for each channel. In this example, create an "Alpha" folder and a "Red & Green" folder, since the red and green channels will be identical.
  2. In the Alpha folder, add a "hue/saturation" adjustment layer and set the saturation to -100.
  3. Add a "brightness/contrast" adjustment layer and darken the image.
  4. Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E to create a merged copy of all the previous layers on a new layer.
  5. Select and copy the new layer.
  6. Create a new document to use as the material map.
  7. Create a new alpha channel in the new document and paste the layer we previously copied.
  8. Return to the original image, delete the merged layer and hide the "Alpha" folder.
  9. Select the "Red & Green" folder, then create a new layer and paint black over any areas that shouldn't be reflective. In this case, the entire body except for the nails and teeth.
  10. Add a "hue/saturation" adjustment layer and set the saturation to -100.
  11. Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E to create a merged copy of all the previous layers on a new layer.
  12. Select and copy the new layer.
  13. Switch to the new document and paste the layer into the Red and Green channels.
  14. Export the image, making sure the "Extra channel as opacity" option is checked.

docs.title: Emission map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "em" (not to be confused with material maps, which end with "m").

Omnimon Alter-B's emission map (chr693a02em.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps BC1 or BC7 sRGB Optional

Tells a material which parts of its surface emit light. The color of each pixel determines the color of the emission. Areas painted black on the texture have no emission.

Left: without emission map. Right: with emission map.

The color of the emission can also be adjusted using the DSTS-EmissiveIntensity material node in Blender. It has three values representing the red, green, and blue channels.

docs.title: Shadow map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "s".

Agumon's shadow map texture (chr050a01s.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps Always BC7 Linear Optional

The RGB values of the texture control shadow color and smoothness. The alpha channel controls the shape of the highlight when the material is glossy.

docs.title: Shadow color
docs.text: The left edge of the texture defines the shadow color, while the right edge defines the light color.

docs.title: Shadow smoothness
docs.text: Shadow maps typically use three colors to achieve a cel-shaded look. More detailed gradients produce smoother or more realistic shadows.

docs.title: Highlight shape
docs.text: The alpha channel (transparency) of the shadow map is used to generate the highlight shape. It is wrapped around a sphere, so a straight line at the top creates a circular highlight. Custom shapes can be added to generate unique highlight effects.

docs.title: Environment map
docs.text:
Textures ending with "env".

The environment map used by most models (chr_env.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps BC1 sRGB Optional

Used when a material has metallic reflections to generate a "chrome" effect. These are special panoramic images made from six squares, each representing a different direction (front, back, left, right, up, down). They wrap around the character and simulate an environment for the reflection. The size of these textures must be 512x384 px, and the "Cube Map from crossed image" option must be checked in Paint.net when exporting the image.

Tip

You can use environment maps to make cool effects, like iridescent materials.

docs.title: Dot sprite
docs.text:
Agumon's dot sprites (dot050.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps None (B5G5R5A1) Linear No

These sprites appear in the summary screen's evolution history, in the Field Guide, and when a Digimon is affected by Crystallization. The compression setting in Paint.net is B5G5R5A1, but it can also be set to B8G8R8A8 (referred to as "compression: none" by Gimp and Photopea) and the game reads them anyway, although the file size is larger (2 kb vs 4 kb).

Dot sprite textures are divided in four sections of 16 x 16 px each: top right and top left contain the idle animation. The bottom-left section contains the attack animation, while the bottom-right section appears when the Digimon is hit by an attack.

docs.title: Profile picture
docs.text:
Agumon's profile picture (ui_chara_icon_1050.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps Always BC7 Linear Always

Used to represent a Digimon in the UI (turn order, box, Field Guide and so on). Here's a video showing how to create the glitch effect for a custom profile picture using Photopea or Photoshop:

Steps
  1. Add a cyan color layer (like #7fadad) and move it to the background.
  2. Duplicate the color layer and put it on top of the main image with ~45% opacity and "color" blend mode to give a faded look.
  3. Duplicate the main image, right click on it, go to Blending Options and uncheck the green channel.
  4. Select the move tool and use the arrow keys (Down Right) to move the copy 5 pixels down and 5 pixels to the right.
  5. (optional) Adjust brightness, contrast or other features if necessary. In this case, I made darker colors slightly lighter.
  6. (optional) Add a shadow to the main image (normal blend mode, full opacity, max "spread", size "0").
  7. Convert the main image into a smart object (so the shadow is included when making the selection in step 8).
  8. Select the pixels of the main image, create an alpha channel (transparency) and fill the selection with white.
  9. Save the image ("extra channel as opacity" must be checked)

This video shows how to remove the glitch effect from an existing profile picture using Photopea or Photoshop:

Steps
  1. Duplicate the image.
  2. Right click on it, go to Blending Options and uncheck the green channel.
  3. Select the move tool and use the arrow keys (Up Left) to move the copy 5 pixels up and 5 pixels to the left.

docs.title: Icons and other UI elements
docs.text:
HP Capsule item icon (ui_icon_item_040.img).

Compression Encoding Mipmaps Always BC7 Linear Optional

Icons should always have mipmaps enabled. Other UI elements (splash screens, Jogmon cards, minimaps, and so on) should have mipmaps enabled only if they're scaled down. Mipmaps help keep them looking smooth at different sizes.

docs.title: Add color and images to text
docs.text: You can add color and images to pretty much any text in the game: item names and descriptions, Field Guide descriptions, skill names and descriptions, NPC dialog, etc.

docs.title: Color
docs.text:
Applying color to an item name.

Use this syntax to give color to your text: {fc#TEXT}

Replace # with by the desired color ID:

ID Color 0 ⬤ Black 1 ⬤ White 2 ⬤ Dark pink 3 ⬤ Green 4 ⬤ Blue 5 ⬤ Yellow 6 ⬤ Magenta 7 ⬤ Teal 8 ⬤ Orange 9 ⬤ Light orange 10 ⬤ Light orange (slightly darker than #9) 11 ⬤ Light blue 12 ⬤ Light yellow 13 ⬤ Yellow (slightly darker than #5) 14 ⬤ Dark pink (slightly lighter than #2) 15 ⬤ Dark gray

Examples

  • {fc6Hello World!} → Hello World!.
  • {fc8Awesome Item:} Defense Up → Awesome Item: Defense Up
  • {fc14Mark} is a {fc7Dinosaur} → Mark is a Dinosaur

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Images are mainly used for icons in skill descriptions, but can be used almost anywhere else. The image must be a square dds file, linear and with mipmaps. BC7 is recomended, but BC1 can also be used. Read more about texture formats here.

The syntax to add images is: {is#}{image(FILENAME)}

# is the image size. The filename must be a texture inside the "images" folder, without image extension, or the game will crash.

Examples

Using a custom texture called smiling_face.dds:

End result Code {is24}{image(smiling_face)} HP Capsule I {is170}{image(smiling_face)} • The Field Guide panel is slightly tilted to the right, so images may look skewed due to the perspective. • To move images, just add line breaks or spaces to the text. {is50}{image(smiling_face)}

Warning

Don't use color codes or images in item_ruby.mbe, since that file use used to sort items, and these codes may break the intended sorting.

docs.title: battle_enemy.mbe
docs.text:
Controls enemy parameters in battle. Includes six CSV files, but to add new enemies we will only use: 000_enemy_parameter.csv, 001_encount_group.csv and 004_battle_enemy_ai.csv.

Abstract

A wild enemy needs: 1. An overworld spawn in field_battle_[map].mbe. 2. A battle group in battle_enemy.mbe/001_encount_group.csv. 3. An enemy entry in battle_enemy.mbe/000_enemy_parameter.csv. 4. An entry in battle_enemy.mbe/004_battle_enemy_ai.csv to determine which skills it can use. 

flowchart TD
A[field_battle_#.mbe] --> |Checks encounter group| B
B[battle_enemy.mbe] --> C[001_encount_group.csv]
C[001_encount_group.csv] --> |Checks enemy data| D
D[000_enemy_parameter.csv] --> |Determines the enemy's overworld model| A
D[000_enemy_parameter.csv] --> |Checks which skills it can use| E
E[004_battle_enemy_ai.csv]

docs.title: 000_enemy_parameter.csv
docs.text:
• int32 0 = unique enemy ID. This value must be the Digimon's ID from digimon_status.mbe, followed by 01. For example Gabumon's ID is 151, so its enemy ID should be 15101.

Info

To create multiple variants of the same Digimon with different parameters for different battles, replace the trailing 01 with 02, 03, and so on. For example, 15102 and 15103 would represent additional variants of Gabumon.

  • int32 2 = base Digimon ID from digimon_status.mbe.
  • int32 5 = Same number used in column int32 0.

docs.title: Enemy battle stats
docs.text:
(Stats used in battle. Overrides base stats from digimon_status.mbe)

  • int32 17 = base HP (at level 1).
  • int32 18 = base SP (at level 1).
  • int32 19 = base ATK (at level 1).
  • int32 20 = base DEF (at level 1).
  • int32 21 = base INT (at level 1).
  • int32 22 = base SPI (at level 1).
  • int32 23 = base SPD (at level 1).

docs.title: Buff Resistance
docs.text: • int32 32 = ID from battle_buff.mbe/001_buff_resist_set.csv. 0 = no buff resistances.

docs.title: Experience and money
docs.text:
• int32 33: base experience gained when the enemy is defeated (at level 1).
  • int32 34: additional experience gained per enemy level.
  • int32 35: base money gained when the enemy is defeated (at level 1).
  • int32 36: additional money gained per enemy level.
Example

The formula is Base money gain + (extra money gain x {current level - 1}). Agumon gives 40 yen at level 1 and grants an additional 4 yen per level. Therefore, at level 10, it grants 76 yen in total (40 + [4 × {10 - 1}] = 76).

Suggested money and experience gains Stage Base EXP Additional EXP Base money Additional money In-training I 4 2 10 1 In-training II 1 1 10 1 Rokie 24 4 40 4 Champion 84 6 80 8 Ultimate 264 8 160 16 Mega 664 10 320 32 Mega + 1364 12 350 35

docs.title: Item drops
docs.text:
• int32 37 = first item dropped when the enemy is defeated (0 = none).
  • int32 39 = first item drop rate (0 to 100).
  • int32 40 = second item dropped when the enemy is defeated (0 = none).
  • int32 42 = second item drop rate (0 to 100).

docs.title: Scan rate
docs.text:
• int32 43 = scan percentage added when the enemy is defeated (0 to 200).
Suggested scan rates Stage Scan rate In-training I 100 In-training II 100 Rookie 20 Champion 15 Ultimate 10 Mega 5 Mega+ 5

Danger

Only Digimon with IDs below 32768 in digimon_status.mbe should be scanned. Otherwise, they will crash the game in the Convert screen. This happens because the game stores scan values as int16 instead of int32, causing IDs above 32767 to overflow.

docs.title: 001_encount_group.csv
docs.text:
Controls the groups of enemies that spawn during a battle. The enemy in the first slot (int32 2) determines the model used by the wild spawn field_battle_map.csv. Even if the battle only has one enemy, it must have an entry in this CSV.

  • int32 0 = unique encounter group ID.
  • int32 2 = first enemy ID (from 000_enemy_parameter.csv).

Danger

The model of the enemy in the first slot must always start with chr or the game will crash.

  • int32 6 = first enemy spawn chance (for the first enemy, always 100 or game crashes).
  • int32 8 = first enemy level.
  • int32 9 = first enemy level in Mega difficulty.
  • int32 10 = first enemy level in Mega + difficulty.
  • int32 14 = second enemy ID.
  • int32 18 = second enemy spawn chance (0 to 100).
  • int32 20 = second enemy level.
  • int32 21 = second enemy level in Mega difficulty.
  • int32 22 = second enemy level Mega + difficulty.
  • int32 26 = third enemy ID.
  • int32 30 = third enemy spawn chance (0 to 100).
  • int32 32 = third enemy level.
  • int32 33 = third enemy level in Mega difficulty.
  • int32 34 = third enemy level Mega + difficulty.
  • int32 38 to int32 74 = fourth to sixth enemy. Unused. Normal battles only allow 3 enemies per battle.
  • string2 75 = lua script used during this battle. (empty) = normal battle, no special scripts, no Surprise Encounters. battle_00000000 = normal battle with 1% chance of getting a Surprise Encounter.
Surprise Encounter odds Digimon Probability PlatinumNumemon 0.35% GoldNumemon 0.30% BlackKingNumemon 0.20% Digitamamon 0.15%
  • int32 80 = battle formation. Determines camera setup and the positioning of enemies during battle. 803 = standard battle formation used by most encounters. 201 = enemies are positioned slightly closer to the player's party. 143 = enemies are positioned slightly farther from the player's party. 121 = enemies are positioned very close to the player's party. 61 = enemies are positioned very far from the player's party.

docs.title: 004_battle_enemy_ai.csv
docs.text:
Determines which skills each enemy can use in battle, either Special Skills or Attachment Skills. Enemies without an entry in this CSV will only use the Attack command. Overrides special skills from digimon_status.mbe.

  • int32 0: unique AI ID. Must be the enemy ID from 000_enemy_parameter.csv, followed by 00. For example Gabumon's enemy ID is 15101, so its AI ID should be 1510100.
  • int32 12: ID of the first skill used by the enemy.
  • int32 14: chance of using the previous skill (0 to 100).
  • int32 18: ID of the second skill used by the enemy.
  • int32 20: chance of using the previous skill (0 to 100).
  • int32 24: ID of the third skill used by the enemy.
  • int32 26: chance of using the previous skill (0 to 100).
  • int32 30: ID of the fourth skill used by the enemy.
  • int32 32: chance of using the previous skill (0 to 100).
  • int32 66: attack skill ID. Must be 10011.
  • int32 68: chance of using the default attack.

docs.title: battle_skill.mbe
docs.text: This MBE manages skills, including both Special Skills and Attachment Skills, as well as item effect skills.

docs.title: 000_battle_skill_list.csv
docs.text:
• int32 0: unique skill ID.

• int32 36: SP cost.

docs.text:
• int32 46 and int16 49: condition.

  • int32 47 and int16 50: effect.

docs.title: 003_skill_mode_change.csv
docs.text:
This CSV controls temporary mode changes in combat, like when Cerberusmon turns into Cerberusmon WM after using Inferno Divide. Triggered in 000_battle_skill_list.csv int32 61.

  • int32 1: ID of the Digimon the user turns into.

Growth pattern IDs
  • 0 = no stat growth. Only used by NPCs.
  • 1 = high HP and ATK growth (Agumon, Guilmon, Veemon, etc.).
  • 4 = high SP and INT growth (Impmon, Lunamon, Renamon, etc.).
  • 7 = high HP, moderate ATK and SPD growth (DemiDevimon, Gabumon, Muchomon, etc.).
  • 10 = high SP, moderate INT and SPD growth (Chuumon, Funbeemon, Kudamon, etc.).
  • 13 = moderate HP, ATK and DEF growth (Hagurumon, Kamemon, Terriermon, etc.).
  • 14 = high overall stat growth from level 1 to 20, then moderate DEF, INT AND SPI increase (only used by Aegiomon).
  • 16 = high SP, moderate INT and SPI growth (Betamon, Kokuwamon, Shamamon, etc.).

Note

For more detailed information, check the CSVs inside digimon_growth.mbe. There's a file for each growth pattern with all the stats gained from level 1 to 99, including some unused ones (5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 15).

docs.title: Special Skills
docs.text:
• int32 72: first Special Skill ID.
  • int32 74: skill slot occupied by the previous skill (always 1).
  • int32 75: second Special Skill ID.
  • int32 77: skill slot occupied by the previous skill (always 2).
  • int32 78: third Special Skill ID.
  • int32 80: skill slot occupied by the previous skill (always 3).
  • int32 81: fourth Special Skill ID.
  • int32 83: skill slot occupied by the previous skill (always 4).

Warning

A Digimon can have up to 12 Special Skills, but adding more than 4 breaks the UI (weird things happen, like being unable to use Attachment Skills). Therefore, the following Special Skill columns (84 to 107) will be ignored and shouldn't be used.

About Special Skill voice lines

Unlike the voice lines for other actions, which can be edited in char_info.mbe, the voice lines for Special Skills are hardcoded. For example, Omnimon will always use the "Transcendent Sword" voice line when using the Special Skill in slot 1, even if that skill isn't actually Transcendent Sword. Therefore, if you're adding a new Special Skill to an existing Digimon, it's best to use an empty slot instead.

docs.text:
Controls evolution lines (determines which Digimon evolves into another).

  • int32 0: unique ID for each evolution.
  • int32 1: ID of the Digimon that will evolve.
  • int32 3: ID of the Digimon it evolves into.
  • int32 5: 0 = normal evolution. 2 = form change.
  • int32 6 to 10: DLC requirement flags. only used by Parallelmon (flag 27500) and the Special Agumon and Gabumon from the Ultimate Edition early unlock (flag 29905).

Info

To calculate De-Digivolution, the game simply reads the evolution entries in reverse. However, form changes work differently: both Digimon must have a corresponding evolution entry pointing to the other.

docs.text:
Controls wild Digimon spawns in the overworld. # represents the map name. For example, Field_npc_d0301.mbe controls all the NPCs in the Abyss Surface (map d0301). It includes two CSV files, but to add new enemies we will only use 001_field_symbol_enemy.csv.

Abstract

A wild enemy needs: 1. An overworld spawn in field_battle_[map].mbe. 2. A battle group in battle_enemy.mbe/001_encount_group.csv. 3. An enemy entry in battle_enemy.mbe/000_enemy_parameter.csv. 4. An entry in battle_enemy.mbe/004_battle_enemy_ai.csv to determine which skills it can use. 

flowchart TD
A[field_battle_#.mbe] --> |Checks encounter group| B
B[battle_enemy.mbe] --> C[001_encount_group.csv]
C[001_encount_group.csv] --> |Checks enemy data| D
D[000_enemy_parameter.csv] --> |Determines the enemy's overworld model| A
D[000_enemy_parameter.csv] --> |Checks which skills it can use| E
E[004_battle_enemy_ai.csv]

docs.title: Basic parameters
docs.text:
• int32 0: unique item ID.

  • int32 6: item category.
Categories

0 = recovery. 1 = enhancements. 2 = special. 3 = skill discs (if an item belongs to this category, it must have an entry in text/skill_ruby.mbe or the game crashes). 4 = equipment (if an item belongs to this category, it must have an entry in 001_equip_parameter.csv). 5 = materials. 6 = farm. 7 = costumes/clothes. 8 = valuables. 9 = cards.

  • int32 7: icon ID. Must be a number from 0 to 99. To know the ID of an icon, check the texture filename ("ui_icon_item_0##.img", the last two digits are the ID).
  • int32 8: item sorting ID. A unique number used for sorting. You can use the same number as the item ID in int32 0.

  • int32 15 and int32 16: overworld effect. -1 in both columns if it can't be used in the overworld. Otherwise, use any of the effects from the list below. Int32 15 contains the effect ID, and int32 16 contains the value related to that effect.
Effect list int32 15 (effect) int32 16 (value) 0 = Uses a skill If "int32 15" is 0, "int32 16" must be -1, and the skill ID set in "int32 13". 3 = Experience Amount of experienge gained. 4 = Bond Amount of bond/friendship gained (multiplied by 100). 9 = Change personality Personality ID (1 to 16). 10 = Move personality (horizontal) Positive values move the personality toward "Heart" (right), while negative values move it toward "Understanding" (left). 11 = Move personality (vertical) Positive values move the personality toward "Companionship" (down), while negative values move it toward "Affection" (up). 12 = Talent Amount of Talent (level cap) gained. 13 = Max HP Amount of HP gained. 14 = Max SP Amount of SP gained. 15 = ATK Amount of ATK gained. 16 = DEF Amount of DEF gained. 17 = INT Amount of INT gained. 18 = SPI Amount of SPI gained. 19 = SPD Amount of SPD gained. 20 = Anomaly points Amount of anomaly points gained.

If you want to create an item that increases SPI by 500, "int32 15" must be 18 and "int32 16" must be 500.

Combining two overworld effects is not fully supported, and some text may display incorrectly.

  • float 10: NPC collision. An invisible sphere around NPCs that blocks movement. 0 = no colission (players can pass through NPCs).
  • float 22: overworld fade out distance. Controls how close the camera can get before the model fades out in the overworld. 0 = the model never fades out.
  • float 26: camera zoom out while riding. 0 = no camera change (used by Terriermon Assistant). 5 = Default (the camera zooms out slightly, used by the rest of the models).
  • string 2 27: second idle animation. Extra animation that occasionally interrupts the normal idle loop. Default: fe02.
  • string 2 29: third idle animation. Empty by default, but any Digimon can use it.
  • string 2 31: fourth idle animation. Empty by default, but any Digimon can use it.
  • Float 33: walking speed while following you in the overworld.

docs.title: Battle
docs.text:
• float 38: Digimon distance from other party members in battle.
  • float_39: player distance from Digimon in battle.
  • int 40 player angle from Digimon in battle (in degrees; 0 = player is in front of the Digimon; 180 = player is behind the Digimon).
  • float 41 fade out distance in battle. Controls how close the camera can get before the model fades out in battle. 0 = the model never fades out.
  • float 43 skill camera distance in battle. Distance of the camera when choosing skills.
  • float_47: shield and buff/debuff size in battle.

docs.title: Model size
docs.text:
• float 56: general scale. Controls the size of the model in all scenarios. It's the size used as the base for the other size columns.
  • float 57: Digifarm scale. Size of the Digimon when it's deposited in the Digifarm.
  • float 58: menu scale. Size of the Digimon in the summary screen and the Field Guide.
  • float 59: map scale. Size of the Digimon when it's following you in the overworld.
  • float 60: battle scale. size of the Digimon in combat.
  • float 61: special skill and victory scale. Sized of the Digimon during the bv# (victory) abd bs# (special skill) animations.
  • float 62: NPC scale. Sized used when the Digimon is added to the overworld as an NPC.
  • float 63: enemy scale in the overworld. Size of the Digimon when it's an enemy in the map outside of battle.

docs.title: Riding
docs.text:
• Float 71: controls if the Digimon is rideable or not. 0 = not rideable. 1 = rideable (flies). 2 = rideable (walks/runs/floats). If the Digimon is rideable, it must have an entry in field_anime.mbe or the game will crash.

Special thanks to: Zeak6464, Slime Doll, Nzerker, Mr. Fanfidoux, Numen.

docs.title: shop.mbe
docs.text:
This MBE controls shop parameters and items available in each shop.

Add shops to NPCs

Shops are added to NPCs through lua script. Open the corresponding NPC lua file and add a new script for that map ID under the OnCheckNPC function: 

elseif talk_id == INTERACTION then
  START_TALK_ACTION_AND_ZOOM(npc_name, true, false)
  CommonShopStart_NoZoomCam(npc_name, SHOPID, "ANIMATION1", "ANIMATION2", "ANIMATION3", "ANIMATION4")
  END_TALK_ACTION_AND_ZOOM(npc_name, true, false)
  Prcs_t30_InvisibleFollower()
- INTERACTION is the NPC interaction ID from field_npc_map.mbe (string2 3). - SHOPID is the shop ID from 000_shop_parameter.csv. - ANIMATION1 is the name of the animation played by the NPC when you interact with it. - ANIMATION2 is the name of the animation played by the NPC when you buy an item. - ANIMATION3 is the name of the animation played by the NPC when you sell an item. - ANIMATION4 is the name of the idle animation used by the NPC (usually bn01).

docs.title: 000_shop_parameter.csv
docs.text:
Basic parameters for each shop.

  • int32 0: unique shop ID.
  • int32 2: shop content. Same ID as the first column. Using the ID of a different shop displays that shop's contents instead.
  • int32 4: unknown. Always 0.
  • int32 8 to int32 16: unknown. Changing the values doesn't seem to have any visible effect.
Add text to a shop

To add text to a shop, it must have four entries in patch_text##/message/field_text.mbe, one for each interaction (greeting, farewell, buy and sell).

  • string2 0: interaction ID: g_shop###_0010_0010 = greeting message . g_shop###_0020_0010 = farewell message . g_shop###_0030_0010 = message displayed when the player buys an item . g_shop###_0040_0010 = message displayed when the player sells an item . (### is the shop ID. It must be at least 3 digits long. If the shop ID has fewer than 3 digits, add leading zeros. For example: 96 → 096.)
  • string 1 character key. Used for the name of the NPC.
  • string 2: message. Maximum 2 lines (any additional lines will appear below the text box instead of inside it).
  • string 3: unknown. Always empty.

docs.title: 001_shop_lineup.csv
docs.text:
Specifies which items are sold in each shop.

  • int32 0: unique lineup ID.
  • int32 1: shop ID.
Some shop IDs

Note

NPCs may have multiple shop IDs with different item catalogs as you progress through the story.

Bartender (In-Between Theater): 91 92 93 94 95 96

Clothing shop (Shinjuku): 9

Dinohyumon (Central Town): 111 115

Gawappamon (Central Town): 121 124

Mushroomon (Central Town): 103

Vademon (Central Town): 101 106

  • int32 3: ID of the item being sold.
  • int32 7: unknown. Always -1.
  • string2 8: flag required for the item to show up. Empty = always visible.

docs.title: How to extract the game data
Containers
docs.text:
All the game assets are stored in the "gamedata" folder. The default path is: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Digimon Story Time Stranger\gamedata

  • .cpk files contain sound and videos .
  • .mvgl files contain everything else: 3D models, databases, textures, etc. .

They are organized in the following way:

  • Files with the app prefix contain all the unpatched base game assets.
  • Files with the patch prefix contain all the assets added through patches.
  • Files with the addcont prefix contain DLC data.
DLC IDs

addcont_01 = episode pack 1 addcont_02 = episode pack 2 addcont_03 = episode pack 3 addcont_05 = Golden Moai farm item addcont_06 = Special Agumon and Gabumon (Early Unlock) addcont_07 = Costume Public Safety Suit & Special Supplies Set addcont_08 = Cyber Sleuth BGM Pack. addcont_09 = Anime Song Pack. addcont_10 = Outer Dungeons The Halls of EXP, Gold, Materials addcont_12 = Cyber Sleuth costume addcont_13 = Swimwear costume addcont_14 = Chosen Children costume addcont_15 = Digimon costume addcont_17 = preorder bonus (Black Agumon and Black Gabumon)

  • Files with the _text## sufix contain text data for the different languages (Digimon names, skill names, UI, dialog, etc.).
Language IDs

text00 = Japanese text01 = English text02 = French text03 = Spanish (Eu) text04 = German text05 = Italian text07 = Portuguese (LatAm) text09 = Korean text10 = Traditional Chinese text11 = Simplified Chinese text30 = Spanish (LatAm)

Examples

  • addcont_17_text00.dx11.mvgl contains Japanese text for the preorder bonus DLC.
  • patch.dx11.cpk contains sound files from patches.
  • app_text01.dx11.mvgl contains English text from the base game.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
There are a variety of tools that can be used to extract the game's data:

  • To extract audio from .cpk files, use CriFsLib (Read how to extract audio).
  • For general file extraction:
Tool Extracts mvgl Unpacks mbe Decompiles lua Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit MVLibrary MVGLTools

docs.title: Extract the game data
docs.text:
With Digimon Time Stranger ToolKitWith MVLibraryWith MVGLTools
  • Download Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit from Github (Code → Download ZIP).
  • Move the zip file to the location where you want to install it, such as a "DSTS Toolkit" folder on your desktop.
  • Extract the contents of the zip into that folder, then run mvgl_tools_gui.exe.
  • Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit's MVGL Tools menu should now open.
  • Change the "operation" to unpack-mvgl.
  • Select the source file (the mvgl file you want to extract) and the target folder (where the extracted content will be saved), then click Execute to start the extraction.
  • Wait until the "operation completed successfully" message appears.
  • Download the latest version of MVLibrary from GitHub (MVLibraryNET.GUI-windows.zip).
  • Move the zip file to the location where you want to install it, such as a "MVLibrary" folder on your desktop.
  • Extract the contents of the zip into that folder, then run MVLibraryNET.GUI.exe.
  • MVLibrary should now open.
  • Drag and drop a .mvgl file from the "gamedata" folder into MVLibrary.
  • Select the files you want to extract → right click → extract
  • Choose a folder to save the extract files.

Tip

To select multiple files, use the Ctrl or Shift keys.

MVGLTools is a command-line tool, so it can be a little bit confusing.

  1. Download the latest version of MVGLTools from GitHub (MVGLTools-v[version]-win64.zip).
  2. Move the zip file to the location where you want to install it, such as a "MVGLTools" folder on your desktop.
  3. Extract the contents of the zip into that folder.
  4. Click the address bar at the top of the window.
  5. Type cmd and press enter.
  6. A black window called Command Prompt will open.
  7. Copy and paste the following command: MVGLToolsCLI.exe --game=dsts --mode=unpack-mvgl "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Digimon Story Time Stranger\gamedata\app_0.dx11.mvgl" "out"
  8. Then press Enter. Wait until the Command Prompt stops processing.
  9. When it finishes, a new folder named out will appear inside the MVGLTools folder with the extracted files.

To extract a different file, change the filename or path from step 7.

Tip

I recommend extracting the app_0 MVGLs first, then extracting the patch MVGLs so the patched files replace the outdated ones.

docs.title: Unpack MBE files
docs.text:
.mbe files contain .csv data tables with various parameteres, including Digimon stats, evolution conditions, skill effects, item information, and more. They are located in the data and text folders inside the .mvgl files.

With Digimon Time Stranger ToolKitWith MVGLTools
  • Extract the .mbe files from the game data.
  • Open Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit. Change the "operation" to unpack-mbe-dir to extract all the .mbe files inside a folder, or to unpack-mbe to extract a single file.
  • Select the source folder/file and the target folder and click the Execute button to start the extraction.

  • Wait until the "operation completed successfully" message appears.

  1. Extract the .mbe files from the game data.
  2. Open the MVGLTools folder.
  3. Create a new folder named mbe inside it, then place all of your .mbe files in that folder.
  4. In the MVGLTools folder, click the address bar at the top of the window.
  5. Type cmd and press enter. This will open a Command Prompt window.
  6. Copy and paste the following command: MVGLToolsCLI.exe --game=dsts --mode=unpack-mbe-dir mbe mbe/out
  7. Then press Enter. Wait until the Command Prompt stops processing.
  8. When it finishes, a new folder named out will appear inside the mbe folder with the extracted CSV files.

docs.title: Edit CSV files
docs.text:
To edit CSV data tables, you can use:

  • Any text editor, like Windows Notepad, or Notepad++ which has some handy CSV plugins.

  • For files with a lot of columns, use LibreOffice Calc. Make sure the character set is Unicode (UTF-8) when opening the files.

If decimal numbers use commas (like 0,5 instead of 0.5), change your region or the data may not work correctly in-game. Go to Tools → Options → Languages and Locales → General, then change the locale setting to "English (USA)". As an alternative to LibreOffice, you can use Modern CSV, though some features are paywalled.

Warning

Do NOT use Microsoft Excel to open CSV files. It changes the column format and causes a lot of problems.

Info

  • Digimon Story: Time Stranger Mod Loader lets the game read unpacked .csv files directly from folders, so you don't need to pack them again. Just place your edited CSV files in a folder with the same name as the MBE file and add it in your mod.

Example

char_info.mbe └─ 000_char_info.csv

  • The .ap prefix appends the content of the .csv file to the original file instead of replacing it.

Example

000_char_info.csv → replaces the original file. 000_char_info.ap.csv → appends its entries to the original file.

If you want to add a new entry, use the .ap prefix. If you want to modify an existing entry, don't use the .ap prefix.

docs.title: Extract sound and videos
docs.text:
With CriFsLib
  • Open CriFsLib.
  • Drag and drop the desired .cpk file into the program.
  • Right click on the desired media file → extract selected. To select multiple files, use the Ctrl or Shift keys.
File types
  • BGM prefix: music .
  • en/voice prefix: English voices and dialog .
  • ja/voice prefix: Japanese voices and dialg .
  • SE prefix: sound effects (UI, skills, etc) .
  • .usm filetype: movies .

docs.title: Play and convert sound files
docs.text: To play the extracted sound files, use Foobar2000 and install vgmstream decoder (file → preferences → components → install). To convert custom sound files into .hca for mods, use Yona.

docs.title: Decompile LUA
docs.text:
.lua files (located in the lua folder) contain scripts. They control NPC interactions, teleports, cutscenes, and so on. Since the game's Lua files are precompiled as Lua 5.2 bytecode, they must be decompiled before they can be edited.

With Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit
  • Extract the LUA files from the MVGLs.
  • Download and install Java.
  • Run lua_decompiler_gui.exe, located in the Digimon Time Stranger ToolKit folder.
  • Select the folder containing the extracted LUA files ("Source Folder"), then choose where you want the decompiled files to be saved ("Output Folder").
  • Click "start decompilation" and wait for the process to finish.
  • You can now open and edit the Lua files in any text editor.

Info

The game can read decompiled .lua files, so you don't need to compile them again.

docs.title: 3D models
docs.text:
3D models consist of three different file types: .geom files contain geometry, bones and materials. .nlst files contain node lists (bone hierarchy, etc.). .anim files contain animations.

To open these files, you must install Blender and one of the following add-ons:

Add-on Imports mesh Imports animations Exports mesh Exports animations Blender version Zeak's 4.5 Romsstar's 4.5 Nymic_Razor's 4.5 Senator John's 5.1 How to install add-ons

Note

In Blender 4.5, instead of an Install button, you'll see a arrow. Click it and select Install from Disk.

Known bugs and limitations
  • Some add-ons are not compatible with each other. Don't install all of them at the same time, or you may encounter errors.
  • Skill effects, particles, lights, texture animations and object collisions can't be edited yet.
  • Time Stranger models contain many unnecessary vertices, which significantly increase the file size. To remove them, enter edit mode, select all and go to Mesh → Clean Up → Delete loose.
  • Some meshes become invisible if they only have 1 weight. Assign a random bone (preferably mvglDummy0000) with a weight of 0.001 to fix it.
  • Edited/custom digimon models may have thicker outlines (workaround).
  • Custom player models can't use train terminals.
  • When using a custom player model, the Palmon you call to travel between floating islands in the Gear Forest will be invisible during the cutscene.
  • If your model has weird shadows, it's likely a weight normalization problem. The sum of all weights must be exactly "1". To fix it, enter weight paint mode and go to weights → normalize all.

docs.title: Textures
docs.text: Textures are in DDS format but use the .img file extension. Simply rename the files to .dds, and you'll be able to edit them with any image editing software (Paint.net, Photopea, etc.). For more information, check the texture documentation.

docs.title: How to install Digimon Story: Time Stranger Mods
Backup your save data
docs.text: Before installing any mods, back up your save data in a safe location in case you want to restore the game to its original, unmodded state. The save files are located in Steam's "savedata" folder. The default path is: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Digimon Story Time Stranger\gamedata\savedata

docs.title: Download Reloaded II
docs.text:
To manage, install and create mods, we will use a program called Reloaded II. It is available in two versions: the original and "II.5 ReMIX"; both have the same features, but II.5 ReMIX includes a UI/UX overhaul and several QOL improvements, like a "check for updates" button. Choose the version you prefer.

Reloaded II (original)Reloaded II.5 ReMIX
  • Download the latest version of Reloaded II from GitHub (release.zip).
  • Move the ZIP file to the location where you want to install it, such as a "Reloaded" folder on your desktop.
  • Extract the contents of Release.zip into that folder, then run Reloaded-II.exe.
  • Reloaded II should now open.

For questions or bug reports, join the Reloaded II Discord. For more information, check the documentation.

  • Download the latest version of Reloaded II.5 ReMIX from GitHub (release.zip).
  • Move the ZIP file to the location where you want to install it, such as a "Reloaded" folder on your desktop.
  • Extract the contents of Release.zip into that folder, then run Reloaded-II.exe.

docs.title: Add Digimon Story Time Stranger to the games list
docs.text:
Reloaded II (original)Reloaded II.5 ReMIX
  • Click the (+) button in the left sidebar.
  • Go to where Digimon Story: Time Stranger is installed. Select the Digimon Story Time Stranger.exe file, then click Save. The Default path is: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Digimon Story Time Stranger\Digimon Story Time Stranger.exe

docs.title: Install DSTS Mod Loader
docs.text:
Next, install Digimon Story: Time Stranger Mod Loader. This dependency allows Reloaded to run mods directly from folders, and also enables the game to read .dds textures without needing to rename them to .img.

  • Download the latest version of Digimon Story: Time Stranger Mod Loader (DSTS.ModLoader[version].7z).
  • Drag and drop the .7z file into Reloaded II. Wait a few seconds and it should appear in the mod list.
Reloaded II (original)Reloaded II.5 ReMIX

Note

docs.title: Gamebanana
docs.text: On GameBanana, mods with 1-Click Install support can be installed just by clicking the "Reloaded II" button.

docs.title: Drag and drop
docs.text: To install a mod from another source, simply drag and drop the mod's .zip or .7z file into Reloaded II, just as you did when installing the Digimon Story: Time Stranger Mod Loader. There are no notifications while mods are installing. Just wait until it finishes and the pop up appears.

docs.title: Manual installation
docs.text:
This is only recommended for big mods (1 GB+) or if drag and drop is not working.

  • Extract the mod files into a new folder.
  • Move that folder into your Reloaded's Mods folder: RELOADED_FOLDER/Mods/
  • Your folders should like: RELOADED_FOLDER/Mods/ExampleMod/ModConfig.json

docs.title: Enable and Disable mods
docs.text: Click the checkbox next to a mod to enable or disable it. A mod is enabled when the checkbox displays a [+], and disabled when the checkbox displays a gray [-].

docs.title: Check if mods are working
docs.text:
• Install Simple Load Checker. It'll edit the intro Bandai Namco logo, making easy to see if mods are working correctly.
  • Make sure all your mods are enabled, then launch the game from Reloaded.

Note

If you get the error "an Application Control policy has blocked this file" while trying to run a game from Reloaded, it's because Windows sometimes blocks it. In that case, you must disable Smart App Control: - In Windows Search, type "Smart App Control" and turn it off. - Or go to Privacy & security → Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control settings. docs.title: Uninstall mods
docs.text:
Reloaded II (original)Reloaded II.5 ReMIX

To uninstall a mod, go to the "Manage mods" button in the left sidebar, choose the mod you want to delete from the list, and click "delete"

To uninstall a mod, simply right click on it and select "delete".

Warning

Before deleting a mod: - If it's an outfit mod, make sure your character is wearing a different outfit, or the game will crash. - If the mod adds a new Digimon and you have it in your party or box, it will turn into an invisible Digimon. You can delete it or leave it in your box, but don't use it in battle or the game will crash. Checking its summary screen may also crash the game in some cases.
